title: Subpage cohort prefetch prototype notes
content:
Context and goal:

This is a working note for a lightweight prototype of a subpage / cohort-based prefetcher for paged KV + fused FlashAttention kernels. Problem we keep hitting: long-tail token sequences cause uneven KV residency (hot prefixes keep full pages resident while many other slots only have a few cache lines touched), which means we pay high latency for page faults during bursty requests.

Hypothesis:
- Grouping requests by a "cohort" key (cohort = model-id + route + prefix-hash-window) and driving prefetch decisions per-cohort yields higher effective hit-rate and fewer small scattered IOs.
- Using a tile-aware probing kernel inside the runtime to predict per-page access density lets us issue coalesced page reads and avoid overfetch.

Design sketch (high level):
1) Cohort formation
   - Cohort key = sha1(model_name + route + prefix_first_128_bytes) >> lowbits (configurable window).
   - Keep a small in-memory table: cohort_id -> recent per-page counters (bloom-like), last_seen_ts, priority_score.
   - On request arrival, look up cohort_id and attach hint to request metadata.

2) Probe + tile scoring kernel (CUDA)
   - Lightweight probe kernel launched on a few warps per SM when a cohort sees first-miss activity after idle.
   - Kernel reads a compact representation of the KV page index (page-level bitmaps / sample of cachelines) and computes a per-page score: score = alpha * recent_hits + beta * predicted_next_n_tokens.
   - Scoring uses warp-wide reductions (cooperative_groups) to allow low-overhead aggregation across threads mapped to contiguous cachelines.
   - Output: ranked page list for cohort -> prefetch planner.

3) Subpage / partial-page prefetching
   - We allow three modes: read-head (small contiguous prefix of a page), stride-chunk (every k-th slab in page), and full-page.
   - Planner picks minimal set of reads to cover top-K scored cacheline ranges with a cost model: cost(io_count, latency) vs expected token-hit savings.

4) Batch-coalesced IO and read scheduling
   - Group page reads from multiple cohorts into coalesced IOs where offset ranges overlap.
   - Issue reads at zone-priority: fast-path for on-host NVMe (async io_uring with io_batch), slower path for cloud object store (range GETs).

5) Eviction and watermarks
   - Cohort score decays exponentially; eviction favors dropping cohorts with low score and pages with low density
   - Introduce a soft-watermark that triggers aggressive prefetch throttling when request-latency SLOs degrade.

Kernel-level details and heuristics to try (proto notes):
- Tile-aware thread mapping: allocate a 2D tile per warp where x maps to cacheline within a page and y maps to candidate pages. This allows single-warp probing of many cachelines with minimal divergence.
- Use 32-bit compressed signatures for cacheline sketches (e.g., top-16 bits of XXHash) to reduce memory footprint in the cohort table.
- Use warp-aggregated atomic counters (one per page) only during the probe window; avoid per-request atomics by staging deltas in shared memory and committing once per block.
- Implement a heuristic "prefetch budget" per cohort per-second to prevent runaway read amplification. Budget tuned by cost model and request tier.

Fused FlashAttention interactions:
- For FlashAttention fused kernels we introduce a prefetch fence point just before KV read-emit path. When kernel launches and sees cohort-prefetch hints, it can block on an in-kernel lightweight spin for prefetch completion if the expected latency is < threshold. Otherwise, kernel continues with fallback slower path that issues on-demand reads.
- Consider a cooperative kernel: small helper kernel (prefetch worker) launched persistently on a subset of SMs to pull pages for active cohorts. This reduces synchronous stalls and lets compute SMs continue. Tradeoff: reduced SM availability and context management.

Experiment plan (minimum viable experiments):
1) Microbench: synthetic prefix distributions with z = 0.7 Zipf and many short tails. Measure page-fault count and avg token latency for baseline (no cohort) vs cohort-prefetch with simple scoring.
2) Kernel perf: compare probe kernel launched per-miss vs persistent helper kernel approach. Measure SM occupancy and overall latency.
3) IO pattern: verify coalesced read counts (IO ops) and bytes read; goal: reduce small IO ops by >= 40% and reduce bytes read by <= 15% relative to full-page overfetch baseline.

Initial prototype constraints (keep it lightweight):
- Implement cohort table in host memory (C++) with lock-free circular buffer for updates; serialize compact table to GPU when probing (single CUDA memcpy).
- Probe kernel only reads compact page index (no full page contents) to avoid long memcpy time.
- Prefetch planner executed on host threadpool to keep kernel small.

Open questions / risks:
- Cohort cardinality explosion: long tail of unique prefixes may create too many cohorts. Mitigation: LRU + hash windowing + sampling.
- IO amplification when cohort heuristics mispredict (false positives) -> can worsen latency. Need conservative defaults and rapid feedback loop.
- Scheduler complexity vs maintainability: adding persistent prefetch workers adds complexity to GPU scheduling and may interfere with regular inference loads.

Short notes on fallback policies and metrics to track:
- Fallback: if prefetch latency > 1.5x expected or missing bandwidth, immediately switch cohort to "on-demand only" for T seconds.
- Metrics: per-cohort page hit-rate, probe-run-duration, prefetch-op-count, bytes_read_by_mode, orphaned_cohorts, avg-inference-latency-with-prefetch, tail-99.9 latency.

Code sketch (pseudo):
- host: record_access(cohort_id, page_id) { local_buffer[cohort_id].push(page_id); if (buffer_len > threshold) schedule_probe(cohort_id); }
- probe kernel: kernel(probe_table_ptr, out_scores_ptr) {
    tile = map_warp_to(tile_x, tile_y);
    load signatures for page_y, cacheline_x;
    compute approx density;
    warp_reduce to page_score;
    write out top-k
 }
- planner: pick set of (page, mode) by greedy covering with cost_model(); issue_coalesced_reads(); notify cohort state.

Short log snippet from a test run (raw):

[2024-11-20 09:11:02] cohort=0x3a2b, first_miss, scheduling probe
[2024-11-20 09:11:02] probe_kernel launched (grid=48, block=128), duration=1.8ms
[2024-11-20 09:11:02] planner picked 6 cacheline ranges -> coalesced into 2 io ops (total bytes=120KB)
[2024-11-20 09:11:02] prefetch complete for cohort=0x3a2b, predicted_hit_rate=0.84
[2024-11-20 09:11:02] flashattn kernel continued; observed token-latency delta=-12.3% vs baseline

Next steps / TODOs:
- Build prototype probe kernel + host table primitives (Ethan owning).
- Wire basic planner and host IO coalescing using existing async IO path (Lucia).
- Run synthetic microbench and compare with patched baseline (Noah).
- If prototype looks promising, we will instrument more cohort metrics and try small persistent prefetch-worker experiment.

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep scoring function simple initially: score = recent_hits + 0.5 * decay_predicted; avoid ML for now.
- Watch out for PCIe/CPU overhead when copying index -> GPU; try to keep index <= 64KB per probe.
- Consider sampling-based index building during compaction instead of full page bitmaps.

References and related work:
- FlashAttention scheduling papers (fast attention via tiling) - see internal reading list
- Prior internal experiment: "stripe-paged-kv-atomic-fusion-rfc" (use ideas for eviction policy but not per-cohort logic)
- External: prefetcher literature (cohort/phase predictors) and OS prefetch heuristics.

End of note.

-- Maya
